output.answer: Broadcom acquired VMware in a cash-and-stock deal announced May 26, 2022, valuing VMware at approximately $61 billion (plus $8 billion of assumed net debt; ~$69 billion total including it), with VMware shareholders electing $142.50 in cash or 0.2520 Broadcom shares per share (50/50 prorated, a 44% premium). The deal closed November 22, 2023 after worldwide regulatory scrutiny — the last approval came from China — ending a months-long saga in which closing was delayed three times; VMware stock then ceased trading on the NYSE and Broadcom shareholders ended up owning ~88% of the combined company. Post-close, Broadcom pivoted VMware around VMware Cloud Foundation (private/hybrid cloud) and moved customers to subscription licensing, prompting antitrust scrutiny in the EU and China, rolling layoffs that reportedly cut VMware's workforce roughly in half by early 2025, and later a partial reversal with a smaller standalone vSphere Express offering.
caveats: Deal value is quoted two ways: ~$61 billion equity value at announcement (Broadcom, May 2022) vs. $69 billion including assumed debt (Reuters, Nov 2023) — both are correct for what they measure.
The layoffs figure (roughly half of VMware's workforce) is Business Insider reporting, not a Broadcom disclosure; exact headcount reduction is unconfirmed.
Post-acquisition licensing changes remain contentious: Bloomberg Law reported fresh EU antitrust scrutiny of Broadcom's VMware practices, so licensing terms and pricing may continue to change.
Per-share consideration value ($138.23) was fixed at the May 25, 2022 Broadcom closing price; actual value at close differed with AVGO's stock price.

passages.quote: Broadcom will acquire all of the outstanding shares of VMware in a cash-and-stock transaction that values VMware at approximately $61 billion, based on the closing price of Broadcom common stock on May 25, 2022. In addition, Broadcom will assume $8 billion of VMware net debt.

VMware shareholders will elect to receive either $142.50 in cash or 0.2520 shares of Broadcom common stock for each VMware share. The shareholder election will be subject to proration, resulting in approximately 50% of VMware's shares being exchanged for cash consideration and 50% being exchanged for Broadcom common stock.
Broadcom Inc. (NASDAQ: AVGO) ... today announced that it has completed its acquisition of VMware, Inc. VMware's common stock will now cease to be traded on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE).
Broadcom on Wednesday closed its $69 billion acquisition of cloud-computing firm VMware after receiving regulatory approval in last major market China and ending a months-long saga.

The European Commission had approved the acquisition after Broadcom offered remedies to help rival Marvell Technology while the UK's Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) gave its green light following an in-depth investigation.
Rolling job cuts by Broadcom have slashed VMware's workforce roughly in half
After pushing customers toward its full private cloud suite, Broadcom is offering a smaller-scale option. But reported pricing could limit its appeal to smaller customers.

key_facts.fact: Broadcom announced an agreement to acquire all outstanding VMware shares in a cash-and-stock transaction valuing VMware at approximately $61 billion, and would assume $8 billion of VMware net debt.

Terms: VMware shareholders could elect $142.50 in cash or 0.2520 Broadcom shares per share, prorated ~50% cash / 50% stock; the $138.23 per-share value was a 44% premium; post-close ownership ~88% Broadcom / ~12% VMware holders; $32 billion committed debt financing.
Broadcom completed the VMware acquisition on November 22, 2023; VMware common stock ceased trading on the NYSE.
Reuters put the deal value at $69 billion and reported it closed after approval in its last major market, China; the closing date had been delayed three times amid global regulatory scrutiny.
The European Commission approved the acquisition after Broadcom offered remedies favoring rival Marvell Technology, and the UK CMA cleared it after an in-depth investigation.

Post-close strategy: Broadcom's focus is enabling private/hybrid clouds, centered on investing in VMware Cloud Foundation, plus Tanzu, Application Networking/Load Balancing, Advanced Security, and VMware Software-Defined Edge.
Rolling layoffs by Broadcom since the acquisition have slashed VMware's workforce roughly in half.

After pushing customers toward the full VMware Cloud Foundation subscription suite, Broadcom introduced vSphere Express, a smaller-scale standalone virtualization option — a partial reversal of its bundle-only licensing approach.
